clue.text: Apply restraint after pound is in a poor state

indicators.note: after places the restraint word behind the pound word

parts.note: to pound is to batter, as a ram does
to shackle is to restrain with fetters

explanation.surface: A prisoner in a bad way after being battered and then chained.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tumbledown or rickety is in a poor state, falling apart.

clue.text: Cross over in switch

indicators.note: the over letter goes inside the switch word

parts.note: a switch is a thin rod or cane

explanation.surface: Moving a cross by flipping a switch.
explanation.definitionFit: A rood is a crucifix, especially one above a church screen.

clue.text: Aimless drifting girl

explanation.surface: A young woman wandering without purpose.
explanation.definitionFit: Melissa is a female forename.

clue.text: Husband querying chef recklessly cycling a lot

indicators.note: recklessly says the letters are thrown about wildly

explanation.surface: A spouse questioning a cook who rides a bike carelessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling' looks like riding a bicycle; it means many oscillations per second.
explanation.definitionFit: High-frequency signals repeat their waves many times each second.

clue.text: Cold picnic item's accompaniment?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: What goes along with a chilled picnic spread.
explanation.definitionFit: Champers is British slang for champagne, a typical drink to go with a hamper.

clue.text: Familiar dobbin shedding coat of dapple-grey

indicators.note: stripping away the outer layers of these words leaves letters hidden within them

explanation.surface: A well-known old horse losing its mottled grey coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Liard is an old word for grey, used of a grey horse.

clue.text: Intermittently visible Neptunian mountain

explanation.surface: A peak on the planet Neptune that comes and goes from view.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily, a famous mountain.

clue.text: Article leads to check for American cop show

indicators.note: leads to puts the article first, followed by the bill word

parts.note: the is the definite article
an American check is a British bill in a restaurant

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece prompting a look at a US police drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bill was a long-running British television police drama.

clue.text: Buff leather got buckles

indicators.note: buckles means bends out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Polished leather that got bent out of shape.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buff' looks like polishing leather; in the buff means naked.
explanation.definitionFit: In the altogether means naked, as does in the buff.

clue.text: Camp has nothing standard

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O
a standard is a banner or flag

explanation.surface: A campsite lacking even a flag on a pole.

clue.text: Skill people used in fitting pad

parts.note: fitting means apt, suitable
art is skill, as in the art of persuasion
men are people

explanation.surface: Craftsmen employed to fit out someone's flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Pad is slang for a home, especially a flat in a block.

clue.text: Turn for instance taking in money making cold calls?

parts.note: a telemark is a skiing turn

indicators.note: the for-instance letters take the money word inside them

parts.note: tin is slang for money

explanation.surface: A ski turn that earns money in freezing conditions.

clue.text: Fling tadpoles out, reducing stress

explanation.surface: Tipping the pond's tadpoles out as a way to relax.
explanation.definitionFit: Soft-pedalling means playing down or de-emphasising something, so reducing its emphasis.

clue.text: Had babysat having arranged time off work

indicators.note: having arranged signals the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A parent who had childminding organised, giving a day's rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sabbath is the weekly day of rest from labour.

clue.text: Non-experts united in shaking a master

indicators.note: the united letter goes inside the rearranged letters
shaking jumbles the letters of a master

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: Novices team up to rattle a master craftsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateurs are untrained people, the opposite of professionals or experts.

clue.text: A cross that's primarily protection against evil

parts.note: a mule is a cross, a hybrid of donkey and horse

indicators.note: primarily picks out the first letter of the word that's

explanation.surface: A crucifix worn chiefly as a guard against wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a charm worn to ward off harm or bad luck.

clue.text: Mexican food producing injury, adult taking sick

indicators.note: taking means the ill word takes on the adult letter after it

parts.note: a tort is a legal wrong or injury
sick means ill
A is the abbreviation for adult, as in film ratings

explanation.definitionFit: A tortilla is a thin flatbread of Mexican cuisine.

clue.text: Support king in northern town

clue.text: Company doctor is good for a laugh

parts.note: a medic is a doctor

explanation.surface: The firm's doctor is a real joker.

clue.text: Bird has soft gold crest

parts.note: P is piano, soft in music
or is gold in heraldry
a ridge is a crest, as of a hill

explanation.surface: A bird with a soft golden crest on its head.

explanation.definitionFit: Porridge is British slang for time served in prison, as is bird.

clue.text: Style of singing succeeded, being brought in by pair on TV

indicators.note: the succeeded letter is placed inside the pair's names

parts.note: Ant and Dec are a British TV presenting duo, giving DEC and ANT
S is the abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a hugely popular British TV double act; here the names run DEC then ANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A descant is a melody sung above the main tune, a style of singing.

clue.text: Misanthrope often portrayed in play but not rep strangely

definitions.text: Misanthrope often portrayed in play but not rep strangely

indicators.note: but not says the letters of rep are to be removed from the pool
strangely says the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hater of mankind, a familiar stage role, though not in repertory theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the letters of MISANTHROPE OFTEN, remove R, E and P, and rearrange the rest. The whole clue also describes the title character.
explanation.definitionFit: Timon of Athens is Shakespeare's play whose hero turns into a bitter hater of humanity.

clue.text: Sort of gaff comprises ordinary item used by fisherman

indicators.note: the flat word comprises, or contains, the ordinary letter

parts.note: gaff is British slang for a home, and a flat is one sort

explanation.walkthrough: 'gaff' looks like a fisherman's hook; it is slang for a place to live.
explanation.definitionFit: A float is the bobbing marker an angler uses to show a bite.

clue.text: Knowing about line in musical film

indicators.note: the knowing word goes about the line letter

parts.note: hep is old slang for knowing, hip

clue.text: Pop fan's hit from 1970s

parts.note: pop is a familiar word for father, daddy
a fan cools, so fan is read as cool

explanation.surface: A father's favourite song from the seventies.

clue.text: Picture that is providing cover for periodical

indicators.note: the that-is letters wrap around the periodical

parts.note: a mag is a magazine, a periodical

explanation.surface: A photograph used as a magazine cover.
explanation.definitionFit: An image is a picture or likeness.

clue.text: Bovine holds source of carbon gas

indicators.note: the animal's name holds the letter inside it

parts.note: a yak is a bovine animal of Tibet

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A cow-like beast that gives off carbon-based gas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gas' looks like methane from the animal; it means idle talk.
explanation.definitionFit: To gas is to chatter at length, and yack is slang for the same.

clue.text: Shepherd's concerned to find this, it's said, really

indicators.note: it's said means the words sound like the answer when spoken

parts.note: a shepherd would look for a stray tup, a lost ram; tup is a ram

explanation.surface: A shepherd anxious to locate something, honestly.
explanation.definitionFit: Straight up is slang for honestly or truly, a way of saying no kidding.
